Metadata.InquiriesOrToReportAnIssue: If you have any questions regarding DermaSensor, their support team is available to help. [SOURCE 1]
Metadata.ReleaseDate: The device was cleared by the FDA in 2024. [SOURCE 5]
Metadata.RegulatoryApprovalStatusIfApplicable: DermaSensor is FDA cleared and CE Marked [SOURCE 4]
Metadata.GlobalAvailability: Available for sale in the U.S. [SOURCE 4]
Metadata.Summary: DermaSensor is an AI-powered, non-invasive, handheld device that assists physicians in evaluating skin lesions for skin cancer. It uses spectroscopy and algorithms to provide an immediate, objective risk assessment. [SOURCE 1, 4, 5]
Metadata.Keywords: Medical Equipment; Skin Cancer; Skin Health; Innovation; Innovative Technology; PCP; Medical Device; Skin Cancer Evaluation

UsesAndDirections.IntendedUseAndWorkflow: The DermaSensor device analyzes suspicious skin lesions using optical spectroscopy and artificial intelligence. It provides an "Investigate Further" or "Monitor" output based on the lesion’s malignancy risk level, aiding in referral decisions. [SOURCE 1]
UsesAndDirections.NecessaryKnowledgeExpertise: The device is intended to be simple and easy to use for physicians. [SOURCE 1]
UsesAndDirections.HowToUse: The DermaSensor device involves a three-step process to analyze suspicious skin lesions and provides results in 30 seconds. [SOURCE 1]

TrustIngredients.ModelType: The DermaSensor device uses a combination of cutting-edge optical spectroscopy and artificial intelligence [SOURCE 1]. The device employs AI-powered, patented optical spectroscopy technologies [SOURCE 4].
TrustIngredients.OutcomesAndOutput: By examining the difference in light scattering, DermaSensor provides an immediate “Investigate Further” or “Monitor,” output based on the lesion’s malignancy risk level [SOURCE 1].
TrustIngredients.TypeAndValueOfSolutionOutput: Provides an immediate, objective risk assessment for all common skin cancers [SOURCE 4, 5].
TrustIngredients.ExplanationForHowAnOutputIsGenerated: The DermaSensor device uses a combination of cutting-edge optical spectroscopy and artificial intelligence to promptly analyze suspicious skin lesions. Our proprietary algorithms, developed and refined over a decade of clinical research, are trained on thousands of diagnosed lesions [SOURCE 1].
TrustIngredients.DevelopmentDataCharacterization: algorithms, developed and refined over a decade of clinical research, are trained on thousands of diagnosed lesions [SOURCE 1].
TrustIngredients.TrainingData: algorithms are trained on thousands of diagnosed lesions [SOURCE 1].
TrustIngredients.SkinToneDiversity: The DermaSensor is beneficial because skin cancers do not always present the same way in people of color [SOURCE 1].
TrustIngredients.RelevanceOfTrainingDataToIntendedPopulat: The device's algorithms were developed and refined over a decade of clinical research, trained on thousands of diagnosed lesions [SOURCE 1].
TrustIngredients.OngoingMaintenance: Customers can manage their devices to see the cloud backups and software updates directly to their DermaSensor [SOURCE 1].
TrustIngredients.TransparencyIntelligibilityAndAccountabi: DermaSensor's algorithm is a locked model, meaning that the version cleared by the FDA is precisely what primary care physicians utilize in their practice [SOURCE 2].
TrustIngredients.FundingSourceOfTheTechnicalImplementatio: DermaSensor has raised $27M prior to Series B financing supported by top institutional investors and medtech entrepreneurs [SOURCE 5].
TrustIngredients.ThirdPartyInformationIfApplicable: DermaSensor offers reimbursement guidance through a partnership with TRG (The Reimbursement Group) [SOURCE 1].

UsefulnessEfficacy.GoalOfMetrics: The DermaSensor device aims to provide physicians with an immediate, objective risk assessment for common skin cancers, improving early detection and timely management of skin cancer [SOURCE 1, 4].
UsefulnessEfficacy.Result: Clinical trial demonstrated 96% sensitivity [SOURCE 2]. Studies found that melanoma detection increased from 70.2% to 79.1%, decreasing missed melanoma from 29.8% to 20.9% [SOURCE 2].
UsefulnessEfficacy.Interpretation: The DermaSensor device provides added security and more data to aid in the management of safety and wellness for patients, increasing referrals and confidence in evaluating skin lesions [SOURCE 1, 2].
UsefulnessEfficacy.TestType: The DermaSensor device utilizes optical spectroscopy and artificial intelligence to analyze suspicious skin lesions [SOURCE 1]. Clinical validation studies have been conducted, with 15 studies to date involving 5,000 lesions scanned and diagnosed [SOURCE 1].
UsefulnessEfficacy.TestingDataDescription: The device has been used in 15 clinical studies and is already in use by hundreds of doctors scanning thousands of lesions a month [SOURCE 5]. The algorithms are trained on thousands of diagnosed lesions [SOURCE 1].
UsefulnessEfficacy.ValidationProcessAndJustification: The DermaSensor device has undergone 15 development, validation, and clinical utility studies to date [SOURCE 1]. It has received FDA De Novo authorization based on a clinical trial involving over 1,000 patients [SOURCE 2].

FairnessEquity.GoalOfMetrics: The DermaSensor device aims to improve skin cancer detection, recognizing that skin cancers do not always present the same way in people of color [SOURCE 1].
FairnessEquity.Interpretation: The DermaSensor device aims to empower physicians with enhanced skin cancer detection skills and provide the best possible care to their patients, including people of color [SOURCE 1].

Resources.ClinicalTrialIfAvailable: The DermaSensor device received FDA De Novo authorization, supported by a clinical trial involving over 1,000 patients, which demonstrated 96% sensitivity [SOURCE 2]. The handheld system has been used in 15 clinical studies [SOURCE 5].
Resources.ReimbursementStatusIfApplicable: DermaSensor offers reimbursement guidance through a partnership with TRG (The Reimbursement Group) [SOURCE 1].
